chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever clashes with Truth would be knocked down by it.

key_terms.الْحَقَّ: the Truth (often referring to God or divine reality)
key_terms.صَارَعَ: to clash, contend, or wrestle with
key_terms.صَرَعَهُ: he knocked him down / he defeated him

ai.seo_question: What happens to those who oppose the Truth according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of wrestling (ṣirāʿ) to illustrate that Truth is not merely an abstract concept but an active, overpowering force. This saying is often cited in Shia theological discourse to affirm the inevitability of divine justice, reminding believers that resistance against Haqq is futile because Truth possesses inherent agency and strength. It serves as both a comfort to the righteous and a warning to the arrogant, emphasizing that the outcome of any struggle is predetermined by the nature of the Truth itself.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 408. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Whoever clashes with Truth would be knocked down by it.
